findings.what: A per-project stored source definition already exists (table repo_map_sources, repoMapSource/setRepoMapSource, keyed by project_directory with include/exclude JSON) and currentRepoMap prefers it over deriveSourceDefinition. The plan says profile.source 'replaces deriveSourceDefinition' and never mentions the existing store, its key (directory vs project key), or migrating it.
findings.failureScenario: A builder adds profile.source beside repo_map_sources, giving two stored definitions for one purpose with different keys; or deletes deriveSourceDefinition although it remains the fallback for projects with no profile (the plan says no profile means work runs as today).
findings.suggestion: State whether profile.source supersedes repo_map_sources (migrate or read-through) and that deriveSourceDefinition stays as the no-profile default.

findings.what: The table omits several Bun-assuming readers that the auto-fix, tool-lookup and recheck rows imply: the allow-list of quality commands in retained-verification/procedure.ts (qualityCommands set of 'bun fmt', 'bun lint --fix', 'bun check', and scoped-format regex at procedure.ts:116), the phase recognizer in src/runner/quality-failure.ts (recognizedVerificationPhases, 'bun run verify', needsMechanicalQualityPreparation), and the hard-coded formatter/lint extension sets and commands in mechanical preparation (runtime.ts:~9460-9490).
findings.failureScenario: Step 2 changes guidance and fix to read the profile, but a cargo or npm project's fix and verify commands are not recognized as quality commands: retained verification rejects the procedure as unsupported and quality failures are not routed to mechanical preparation.
findings.suggestion: Name procedure.ts and quality-failure.ts as readers of verify/fix, and list them in build steps 2 and 4.

findings.what: The recheck is more Node-shaped than 'install command, variables, lockfiles'. isolation.ts builds around a node_modules symlink and tree ownership checks (assertOwnedDependencyTree, node_modules paths at 565, 713, 910, 1027, 1047) and passes Bun-specific flags (--frozen-lockfile, --ignore-scripts, --no-save, --no-progress). Cargo has no node_modules, and `cargo fetch` populates a registry in CARGO_HOME, not the workspace.
findings.failureScenario: A builder swaps in profile.install and the lockfile list, then finds isolation still demands a node_modules tree and a Bun on PATH, so a cargo recheck cannot pass or silently runs without isolated dependencies.
findings.suggestion: Add to step 4 what dependency isolation means for a toolchain with no node_modules (what is linked or owned), and that the Bun flags move into the Bun profile's install string.

findings.what: `verify` items carry only id and command, but the code that runs checks attaches per-check timing (inactivity and hard timeout defaults, amendments) and the test hang guard is a rewrite of command text. The profile has no field for timeouts, and the table says the hang guard 'becomes part of a Bun profile's commands' while test-hang-guard.ts rewrites commands at run time for any author-written `bun test`.
findings.failureScenario: Builder bakes `--timeout 120000` into the stored command, then withTestHangGuard and the profile disagree about who owns the flag; non-Bun profiles get no hang protection with no stated reason.
evidence: plan: "Bun test hang guard | becomes part of a Bun profile's commands"
findings.suggestion: Decide whether withTestHangGuard is deleted or stays, and say verify timing stays on the existing defaults.

findings.what: Fallow already has a per-project stored config and entry-point/ignore settings (getLatestFallowConfig, setFallowConfig, hasStoredFallowConfig) that the config gate reads. The plan's `audit: off` and `source` must interact with it, but the plan names neither this store nor review-git.ts's hardcoded SOURCE_EXTENSIONS/CONFIG_FILES/BASE_TREE_PATHSPECS (the 'does this change matter' check) as what changes. runtime.ts:5767 and 7920 are the gate call sites.
findings.failureScenario: Builder gates only fallowConfigGate on audit; the review-git extension list still marks .rs-only changes irrelevant or relevant by JS rules, and base-tree materialisation still fetches only JS/CSS/JSON pathspecs.
findings.suggestion: List review-git.ts and fallow-gate.ts call sites in step 5; say whether source.include replaces SOURCE_EXTENSIONS.

findings.what: The plan says the runtime split moves verification modules first so steps 2 and 4 build on them, but gives no edge or status: the split plan lives in .agents/plans/runtime-split.md and, per runtime.ts still holding mechanical preparation (R21) at runtime.ts:9465+, has not landed. Steps 2 and 4 would otherwise edit the 12k-line runtime.ts concurrently with the split.
findings.failureScenario: Steps 2 and 4 are built against runtime.ts while the split moves the same ranges (R21 verification candidate, R24 effect reconciliation), producing conflicting edits or edits to code that has moved.
findings.suggestion: Make steps 2 and 4 depend on the split's verification-candidate and effect-reconciliation units, and link the split plan.

questions.question: Should a project with a stored repo_map_sources row keep it when a profile is created, or should the profile's source supersede it?
questions.why: Decides whether repo_map_sources is migrated and dropped or left as a second source of truth.
options: profile.source supersedes; migrate existing rows into the profile on first setup
repo_map_sources stays and profile.source is read only when no row exists
drop repo_map_sources and keep only the derived default plus profile

questions.question: For a toolchain without node_modules (cargo), should the isolated recheck still provide an isolated dependency directory, and if so which one?
questions.why: Determines whether step 4 reworks isolation.ts's dependency-tree model or only swaps the install command.
options: Isolation owns a per-toolchain dependency directory declared in the profile (node_modules, target)
Isolation covers node_modules only; non-Node profiles run install in the candidate workspace with CARGO_HOME from env
Non-Node profiles skip dependency isolation and rely on a clean workspace
